screening.reason: Randomized placebo-controlled live-probiotic trial in biopsy-confirmed NAFLD, published before the cutoff. At 3 months, probiotic-group ALT was reported as 60.4 ± 30.4 UI/L; dispersion type is unspecified. Control endpoint ALT is absent from the supplied abstract.

records.extraction_reason: Published in 2011, this double-blind parallel randomized placebo-controlled trial enrolled humans with biopsy-confirmed NAFLD, excluded other causes of liver disease, and compared a probiotic containing Lactobacillus bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus with starch placebo for 3 months.

screening.reason: Randomized placebo-controlled trial of live Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG for 8 weeks in children with ultrasonographic fatty liver; other liver diseases excluded. Numerical end-treatment ALT is not supplied; only a between-group ALT variation P value of 0.03 is reported.

Randomized trial in biopsy-assessed NASH comparing Bifidobacterium longum plus fructo-oligosaccharides and lifestyle modification with lifestyle modification alone for 24 weeks. ALT was assessed, but numerical end-treatment ALT is not supplied.

records.extraction_reason: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel trial in adults with biopsy-confirmed NASH, excluding other causes of liver disease. Bifidobacterium longum with fructo-oligosaccharides was administered for 24 weeks alongside lifestyle modification. Published online before 2013-06-30.

screening.reason: Randomized live-probiotic versus usual-care trial in histology-proven NASH, published before the cutoff. Treatment lasted 6 months; endpoint ALT is not reported in the supplied abstract.

records.extraction_reason: NCT00870012 is a randomized parallel trial in 20 adults with histology-proven NASH, comparing live probiotics plus prebiotics with usual care for 6 months. Other liver disease causes were excluded, and publication preceded 2013-06-30. Eligibility is independent of unavailable ALT endpoint statistics.

screening.reason: Placebo-controlled randomized trial in type 2 diabetes, but the abstract does not establish whether brewer's yeast was a probiotic or report end-treatment fasting glucose. Full text was not supplied to verify eligibility.

records.extraction_reason: Randomized placebo-controlled trial in people with type 2 diabetes, but the intervention was inactivated brewer’s yeast rather than probiotic supplementation. The article states: “Brewer’s yeast supplements or nutritional yeasts are dried and inactivated yeast cells called ‘Saccharomyces cerevisiae’ which have lost their fermentation activity.” Trial registry ID: IRCT138807062513N1.
missing_numeric_evidence: End-of-treatment FBG means and SDs are not reported in the supplied article; this is separate from the intervention-based exclusion.
